    "answerable": [
      "Simulate spatially variable recharge (drainage flux below root zone) across the Naches elevation and climate gradient using ELM single-column runs.",

    "not_answerable": [
      "Confirming that recharge is 'exactly 500 mm/yr everywhere' — this premise is physically implausible across a 352-1977 m elevation range with strong precipitation/temperature gradients, and cannot be validated because NO direct recharge measurements exist in the domain.",

    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 4,
  "n_justification": "The claim of uniform recharge is best tested by sampling the strong orographic gradient (352-1977 m) rather than a single point. Four columns span low-elevation valley to high-elevation snow-dominated headwaters, with contrasting soil textures, allowing the spatial variability of modeled recharge to be quantified and directly compared to the asserted uniform 500 mm/yr.",
  "columns": [
    {"id": "naches_valley_low", "lat": 46.75, "lon": -120.55, "soil_texture": "sandy_loam"},
    {"id": "naches_midslope", "lat": 46.85, "lon": -120.95, "soil_texture": "loam"},
    {"id": "naches_upland_forest", "lat": 46.95, "lon": -121.20, "soil_texture": "silt_loam"},
    {"id": "naches_headwater_high", "lat": 46.60, "lon": -121.40, "soil_texture": "gravelly_loam"}
  ],
  "elm_config": {
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_START": "1980",
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_END": "2018",
    "STOP_N": "39",
    "RUN_STARTDATE": "1980-01-01",
    "hist_variables": [
      "QDRAI",

      "EFLX_LH_TOT",

  },
  "requires_capabilities": [
    "ELM single-column (PTS_MODE) point simulations",
    "GSWP3/CRUNCEP or ELM-compatible atmospheric forcing 1980-2018 with orographic downscaling",
    "SSURGO/gridded soil texture assignment per column",
    "PFLOTRAN coupling (optional) for saturated-zone recharge partitioning consistency check",
    "Fan 2013 water-table depth prior and USGS well levels for proxy evaluation of steady-state moisture/WTD"

  "assumptions": [
    "PREMISE FLAGGED: The assertion that recharge is 'exactly 500 mm/yr everywhere' is treated as a hypothesis to be tested, not a fact to be confirmed; strong elevation and precipitation gradients make spatially uniform recharge highly unlikely.",
    "Recharge is diagnosed as the multi-year mean bottom-boundary drainage flux (QDRAI/QRECHARGE) below the rooting zone; ELM has no explicit deep-aquifer recharge observation to calibrate against.",

answerable: Simulate spatially variable recharge (drainage flux below root zone) across the Naches elevation and climate gradient using ELM single-column runs.
Test sensitivity of recharge to soil texture and meteorological forcing.
Report the distribution of modeled recharge and compare it against the claimed 500 mm/yr value.
not_answerable: Confirming that recharge is 'exactly 500 mm/yr everywhere' — this premise is physically implausible across a 352-1977 m elevation range with strong precipitation/temperature gradients, and cannot be validated because NO direct recharge measurements exist in the domain.
Any true validation of recharge magnitude, since observations_missing includes recharge measurements; only water-table (Fan 2013 WTD, USGS wells) proxies are available.

parsed.n_justification: The claim of uniform recharge is best tested by sampling the strong orographic gradient (352-1977 m) rather than a single point. Four columns span low-elevation valley to high-elevation snow-dominated headwaters, with contrasting soil textures, allowing the spatial variability of modeled recharge to be quantified and directly compared to the asserted uniform 500 mm/yr.
requires_capabilities: GSWP3/CRUNCEP or ELM-compatible atmospheric forcing 1980-2018 with orographic downscaling
SSURGO/gridded soil texture assignment per column
PFLOTRAN coupling (optional) for saturated-zone recharge partitioning consistency check
Fan 2013 water-table depth prior and USGS well levels for proxy evaluation of steady-state moisture/WTD
assumptions: PREMISE FLAGGED: The assertion that recharge is 'exactly 500 mm/yr everywhere' is treated as a hypothesis to be tested, not a fact to be confirmed; strong elevation and precipitation gradients make spatially uniform recharge highly unlikely.
Recharge is diagnosed as the multi-year mean bottom-boundary drainage flux (QDRAI/QRECHARGE) below the rooting zone; ELM has no explicit deep-aquifer recharge observation to calibrate against.
A 39-year run (1980-2018) with the first ~5 years discarded as spin-up provides climatological mean recharge; additional accelerated-decomposition spin-up is applied beforehand.
Soil textures are assigned from best-available gridded soil data per column and are one of the two candidate drivers explicitly perturbed.
Because no direct recharge observations exist, results are reported as modeled estimates with uncertainty ranges, not as confirmation of the 500 mm/yr figure.
Water-table proxies (USGS wells, Fan 2013) are used only as weak consistency checks on soil-moisture/WTD behavior, not as recharge validation.
